text: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.
clarifications: For example, find the approximate probability that a spinning penny will land heads up or that a tossed paper cup will land open-end down. Do the outcomes for the spinning penny appear to be equally likely based on the observed frequencies?
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.
clarifications: For example, use random digits as a simulation tool to approximate the answer to the question: If 40% of donors have type A blood, what is the probability that it will take at least 4 donors to find one with type A blood?
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Know and apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent numerical expressions.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use square root and cube root symbols to represent solutions to equations of the form x² = p and x³ = p, where p is a positive rational number. Evaluate square roots of small perfect squares and cube roots of small perfect cubes. Know that √2 is irrational.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use numbers expressed in the form of a single digit times an integer power of 10 to estimate very large or very small quantities, and to express how many times as much one is than the other.
clarifications: For example, estimate the population of the United States as 3 × 108 and the population of the world as 7 × 109, and determine that the world population is more than 20 times larger.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Perform operations with numbers expressed in scientific notation, including problems where both decimal and scientific notation are used. Use scientific notation and choose units of appropriate size for measurements of very large or very small quantities (e.g., use millimeters per year for seafloor spreading). Interpret scientific notation that has been generated by technology.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Graph proportional relationships, interpreting the unit rate as the slope of the graph. Compare two different proportional relationships represented in different ways.
clarifications: For example, compare a distance-time graph to a distance-time equation to determine which of two moving objects has greater speed.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use similar triangles to explain why the slope m is the same between any two distinct points on a non-vertical line in the coordinate plane; derive the equation y = mx for a line through the origin and the equation y = mx + b for a line intercepting the vertical axis at b.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Solve linear equations in one variable.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Give examples of linear equations in one variable with one solution, infinitely many solutions, or no solutions. Show which of these possibilities is the case by successively transforming the given equation into simpler forms, until an equivalent equation of the form x = a, a = a, or a = b results (where a and b are different numbers).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Solve linear equations with rational number coefficients, including equations whose solutions require expanding expressions using the distributive property and collecting like terms.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Understand that solutions to a system of two linear equations in two variables correspond to points of intersection of their graphs, because points of intersection satisfy both equations simultaneously.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Solve systems of two linear equations in two variables algebraically, and estimate solutions by graphing the equations. Solve simple cases by inspection.
clarifications: For example, 3x + 2y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 6 have no solution because 3x + 2y cannot simultaneously be 5 and 6.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Solve real-world and mathematical problems leading to two linear equations in two variables.
clarifications: For example, given coordinates for two pairs of points, determine whether the line through the first pair of points intersects the line through the second pair.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Understand that a function is a rule that assigns to each input exactly one output. The graph of a function is the set of ordered pairs consisting of an input and the corresponding output.
clarifications: Function notation is not required in Grade 8.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Compare properties of two functions each represented in a different way (algebraically, graphically, numerically in tables, or by verbal descriptions).
clarifications: For example, given a linear function represented by a table of values and a linear function represented by an algebraic expression, determine which function has the greater rate of change.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Interpret the equation y = mx + b as defining a linear function, whose graph is a straight line; give examples of functions that are not linear.
clarifications: For example, the function A = s² giving the area of a square as a function of its side length is not linear because its graph contains the points (1,1), (2,4) and (3,9), which are not on a straight line.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Construct a function to model a linear relationship between two quantities. Determine the rate of change and initial value of the function from a description of a relationship or from two (x, y) values, including reading these from a table or from a graph. Interpret the rate of change and initial value of a linear function in terms of the situation it models, and in terms of its graph or a table of values.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Describe qualitatively the functional relationship between two quantities by analyzing a graph (e.g., where the function is increasing or decreasing, linear or nonlinear). Sketch a graph that exhibits the qualitative features of a function that has been described verbally.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Verify experimentally the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations:
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Lines are taken to lines, and line segments to line segments of the same length.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Angles are taken to angles of the same measure.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Parallel lines are taken to parallel lines.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is congruent to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, and translations; given two congruent figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the congruence between them.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Describe the effect of dilations, translations, rotations, and reflections on two-dimensional figures using coordinates.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Understand that a two-dimensional figure is similar to another if the second can be obtained from the first by a sequence of rotations, reflections, translations, and dilations; given two similar two-dimensional figures, describe a sequence that exhibits the similarity between them.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use informal arguments to establish facts about the angle sum and exterior angle of triangles, about the angles created when parallel lines are cut by a transversal, and the angle-angle criterion for similarity of triangles.
clarifications: For example, arrange three copies of the same triangle so that the sum of the three angles appears to form a line, and give an argument in terms of transversals why this is so.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to determine unknown side lengths in right triangles in real-world and mathematical problems in two and three dimensions.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Apply the Pythagorean Theorem to find the distance between two points in a coordinate system.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Know the formulas for the volumes of cones, cylinders, and spheres and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Know that numbers that are not rational are called irrational. Understand informally that every number has a decimal expansion; for rational numbers show that the decimal expansion repeats eventually, and convert a decimal expansion which repeats eventually into a rational number.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use rational approximations of irrational numbers to compare the size of irrational numbers, locate them approximately on a number line diagram, and estimate the value of expressions (e.g., π²).
clarifications: For example, by truncating the decimal expansion of √2, show that √2 is between 1 and 2, then between 1.4 and 1.5, and explain how to continue on to get better approximations.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Construct and interpret scatter plots for bivariate measurement data to investigate patterns of association between two quantities. Describe patterns such as clustering, outliers, positive or negative association, linear association, and nonlinear association.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Know that straight lines are widely used to model relationships between two quantitative variables. For scatter plots that suggest a linear association, informally fit a straight line, and informally assess the model fit by judging the closeness of the data points to the line.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use the equation of a linear model to solve problems in the context of bivariate measurement data, interpreting the slope and intercept.
clarifications: For example, in a linear model for a biology experiment, interpret a slope of 1.5 cm/hr as meaning that an additional hour of sunlight each day is associated with an additional 1.5 cm in mature plant height.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Understand that patterns of association can also be seen in bivariate categorical data by displaying frequencies and relative frequencies in a two-way table. Construct and interpret a two-way table summarizing data on two categorical variables collected from the same subjects. Use relative frequencies calculated for rows or columns to describe possible association between the two variables.
clarifications: For example, collect data from students in your class on whether or not they have a curfew on school nights and whether or not they have assigned chores at home. Is there evidence that those who have a curfew also tend to have chores?
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
text: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
text: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x — a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x — a) is a factor of p(x).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
text: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
text: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.
clarifications: For example, the polynomial identity (x² + y²)2 = (x² — y²)² + (2xy)² can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
text: (+) Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)n in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal's Triangle.
clarifications: The Binomial Theorem can be proved by mathematical induction or by a combinatorial argument.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
text: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write a(x /b(x) in the form q(x) + r(x)/b(x), where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions
text: (+) Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.
clarifications: For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.
clarifications: For example, rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: 10. Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: 11. Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.★
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: 12. Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x — p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.
clarifications: For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = -3x and the circle x² + y² = 3.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation in a vector variable.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Interpret expressions that represent a quantity in terms of its context ★
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Interpret parts of an expression, such as terms, factors, and coefficients.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Interpret complicated expressions by viewing one or more of their parts as a single entity.
clarifications: For example, interpret P(1+r)n as the product of P and a factor not depending on P.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use the structure of an expression to identify ways to rewrite it.
clarifications: For example, see x4 — y4 as (x²)² — (y²)², thus recognizing it as a difference of squares that can be factored as (x² — y²)(x² + y²).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Choose and produce an equivalent form of an expression to reveal and explain properties of the quantity represented by the expression.★
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Factor a quadratic expression to reveal the zeros of the function it defines.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Complete the square in a quadratic expression to reveal the maximum or minimum value of the function it defines.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use the properties of exponents to transform expressions for exponential functions.
clarifications: For example the expression 1.15t can be rewritten as (1.151/12)12t  1.01212t to reveal the approximate equivalent monhly interest rate if the annual rate is 15%.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.★
clarifications: For example, calculate mortgage payments.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Write a function that describes a relationship between two quantities ★
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Determine an explicit expression, a recursive process, or steps for calculation from a context.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Combine standard function types using arithmetic operations.
clarifications: For example, build a function that models the temperature of a cooling body by adding a constant function to a decaying exponential, and relate these functions to the model.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Compose functions.
clarifications: For example, if T(y) is the temperature in the atmosphere as a function of height, and h(t) is the height of a weather balloon as a function of time, then T(h(t)) is the temperature at the location of the weather balloon as a function of time.

text: Analyze and compare two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts (e.g., number of sides and vertices/"corners") and other attributes (e.g., having sides of equal length).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Model shapes in the world by building shapes from components (e.g., sticks and clay balls) and drawing shapes.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes.
clarifications: For example, "Can you join these two triangles with full sides touching to make a rectangle?"
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Describe measurable attributes of objects, such as length or weight. Describe several measurable attributes of a single object.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Directly compare two objects with a measurable attribute in common, to see which object has "more of"/"less of" the attribute, and describe the difference.
clarifications: For example, directly compare the heights of two children and describe one child as taller/shorter.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Classify objects into given categories; count the numbers of objects in each category and sort the categories by count.
clarifications: Limit category counts to be less than or equal to 10.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten
text: Compose and decompose numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and some further ones, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each composition or decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 18 = 10 + 8); understand that these numbers are composed of ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Represent addition and subtraction with objects, fingers, mental images, drawings, sounds (e.g., claps), acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, or equations.
clarifications: Drawings need not show details, but should show the mathematics in the problem (This applies wherever drawings are mentioned in the Standards.)
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Solve addition and subtraction word problems, and add and subtract within 10, e.g., by using objects or drawings to represent the problem.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record each decomposition by a drawing or equation (e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number, e.g., by using objects or drawings, and record the answer with a drawing or equation.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Fluently add and subtract within 5.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Reason abstractly and quantitatively.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Model with mathematics.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use appropriate tools strategically.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Attend to precision.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Look for and make use of structure.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Know there is a complex number i such that i² = —1, and every complex number has the form a + bi with a and b real.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use the relation i² = —1 and the commutative, associative, and distributive properties to add, subtract, and multiply complex numbers.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Find the conjugate of a complex number; use conjugates to find moduli and quotients of complex numbers.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Represent complex numbers on the complex plane in rectangular and polar form (including real and imaginary numbers), and explain why the rectangular and polar forms of a given complex number represent the same number.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Represent addition, subtraction, multiplication, and conjugation of complex numbers geometrically on the complex plane; use properties of this representation for computation.
clarifications: For example, (-1 + √3 i)³ = 8 because (-1 + √3 i) has modulus 2 and argument 120°.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Calculate the distance between numbers in the complex plane as the modulus of the difference, and the midpoint of a segment as the average of the numbers at its endpoints.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Solve quadratic equations with real coefficients that have complex solutions.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Extend polynomial identities to the complex numbers.
clarifications: For example, rewrite x² + 4 as (x + 2i)(x - 2i).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Know the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra; show that it is true for quadratic polynomials.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use units as a way to understand problems and to guide the solution of multi-step problems; choose and interpret units consistently in formulas; choose and interpret the scale and the origin in graphs and data displays.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Define appropriate quantities for the purpose of descriptive modeling.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to limitations on measurement when reporting quantities.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents.
clarifications: For example, we define 51/3 to be the cube root of 5 because we want (51/3)³ = 5(1/3)³ to hold, so (51/3)³ must equal 5.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Rewrite expressions involving radicals and rational exponents using the properties of exponents.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Explain why the sum or product of two rational numbers is rational; that the sum of a rational number and an irrational number is irrational; and that the product of a nonzero rational number and an irrational number is irrational.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Recognize vector quantities as having both magnitude and direction. Represent vector quantities by directed line segments, and use appropriate symbols for vectors and their magnitudes (e.g., v, |v|, ||v||, v).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: 10. (+) Understand that the zero and identity matrices play a role in matrix addition and multiplication similar to the role of 0 and 1 in the real numbers. The determinant of a square matrix is nonzero if and only if the matrix has a multiplicative inverse.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Multiply a vector (regarded as a matrix with one column) by a matrix of suitable dimensions to produce another vector. Work with matrices as transformations of vectors.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Work with 2 × 2 matrices as transformations of the plane, and interpret the absolute value of the determinant in terms of area.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Find the components of a vector by subtracting the coordinates of an initial point from the coordinates of a terminal point.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Solve problems involving velocity and other quantities that can be represented by vectors.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Add and subtract vectors.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Add vectors end-to-end, component-wise, and by the parallelogram rule. Understand that the magnitude of a sum of two vectors is typically not the sum of the magnitudes.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Given two vectors in magnitude and direction form, determine the magnitude and direction of their sum.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Understand vector subtraction v — w as v + (—w), where —w is the additive inverse of w, with the same magnitude as w and pointing in the opposite direction. Represent vector subtraction graphically by connecting the tips in the appropriate order, and perform vector subtraction component-wise.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Multiply a vector by a scalar.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Represent scalar multiplication graphically by scaling vectors and possibly reversing their direction; perform scalar multiplication component-wise, e.g., as c(vx, vy) = (cvx, cvy).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Compute the magnitude of a scalar multiple cv using ||cv|| = |c|v. Compute the direction of cv knowing that when |c|v ? 0, the direction of cv is either along v (for c > 0) or against v (for c < 0).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Use matrices to represent and manipulate data, e.g., to represent payoffs or incidence relationships in a network.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Multiply matrices by scalars to produce new matrices, e.g., as when all of the payoffs in a game are doubled.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Add, subtract, and multiply matrices of appropriate dimensions.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Understand that, unlike multiplication of numbers, matrix multiplication for square matrices is not a commutative operation, but still satisfies the associative and distributive properties.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
text: Describe events as subsets of a sample space (the set of outcomes) using characteristics (or categories) of the outcomes, or as unions, intersections, or complements of other events ("or," "and," "not").
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
text: Understand that two events A and B are independent if the probability of A and B occurring together is the product of their probabilities, and use this characterization to determine if they are independent.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
text: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
text: Construct and interpret two-way frequency tables of data when two categories are associated with each object being classified. Use the two-way table as a sample space to decide if events are independent and to approximate conditional probabilities.
clarifications: For example, collect data from a random sample of students in your school on their favorite subject among math, science, and English. Estimate the probability that a randomly selected student from your school will favor science given that the student is in tenth grade. Do the same for other subjects and compare the results.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
text: Recognize and explain the concepts of conditional probability and independence in everyday language and everyday situations.
clarifications: For example, compare the chance of having lung cancer if you are a smoker with the chance of being a smoker if you have lung cancer.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
text: Find the conditional probability of A given B as the fraction of B's outcomes that also belong to A, and interpret the answer in terms of the model.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
text: Apply the Addition Rule, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) — P(A and B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
text: (+) Apply the general Multiplication Rule in a uniform probability model, P(A and B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B), and interpret the answer in terms of the model.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
text: (+) Use permutations and combinations to compute probabilities of compound events and solve problems.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Understand statistics as a process for making inferences about population parameters based on a random sample from that population.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Decide if a specified model is consistent with results from a given data-generating process, e.g., using simulation.
clarifications: For example, a model says a spinning coin falls heads up with probability 0.5. Would a result of 5 tails in a row cause you to question the model?
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Recognize the purposes of and differences among sample surveys, experiments, and observational studies; explain how randomization relates to each.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use data from a sample survey to estimate a population mean or proportion; develop a margin of error through the use of simulation models for random sampling.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use data from a randomized experiment to compare two treatments; use simulations to decide if differences between parameters are significant.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Evaluate reports based on data.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Represent data with plots on the real number line (dot plots, histograms, and box plots).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center (median, mean) and spread (interquartile range, standard deviation) of two or more different data sets.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data sets, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Summarize categorical data for two categories in two-way frequency tables. Interpret relative frequencies in the context of the data (including joint, marginal, and conditional relative frequencies). Recognize possible associations and trends in the data.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Represent data on two quantitative variables on a scatter plot, and describe how the variables are related.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Fit a function to the data; use functions fitted to data to solve problems in the context of the data.
clarifications: Use given functions or choose a function suggested by the context. Emphasize linear, quadratic, and exponential models.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Informally assess the fit of a function by plotting and analyzing residuals.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Fit a linear function for a scatter plot that suggests a linear association.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Interpret the slope (rate of change) and the intercept (constant term) of a linear model in the context of the data.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Compute (using technology) and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Distinguish between correlation and causation.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Define a random variable for a quantity of interest by assigning a numerical value to each event in a sample space; graph the corresponding probability distribution using the same graphical displays as for data distributions.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Calculate the expected value of a random variable; interpret it as the mean of the probability distribution.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which theoretical probabilities can be calculated; find the expected value.
clarifications: For example, find the theoretical probability distribution for the number of correct answers obtained by guessing on all five questions of a multiple-choice test where each question has four choices, and find the expected grade under various grading schemes.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Develop a probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which probabilities are assigned empirically; find the expected value.
clarifications: For example, find a current data distribution on the number of TV sets per household in the United States, and calculate the expected number of sets per household. How many TV sets would you expect to find in 100 randomly selected households?
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Weigh the possible outcomes of a decision by assigning probabilities to payoff values and finding expected values.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Find the expected payoff for a game of chance.
clarifications: For example, find the expected winnings from a state lottery ticket or a game at a fast-food restaurant.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: Evaluate and compare strategies on the basis of expected values.
clarifications: For example, compare a high-deductible versus a low-deductible automobile insurance policy using various, but reasonable, chances of having a minor or a major accident.
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Use probabilities to make fair decisions (e.g., drawing by lots, using a random number generator).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.

subject: Math
text: (+) Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts (e.g., product testing, medical testing, pulling a hockey goalie at the end of a game).
source_doc: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics — © Copyright 2010. National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and Council of Chief State School Officers. All rights reserved.
